entry.title: Designing Model Ensembles in GenAI Platforms
entry.summary: The Limitations of the Monolithic Model Approach In the early stages of Generative AI adoption, the standard pattern was to select a single high-parameter model and optimize prompts for it. However, for production-grade systems, relying on a single model creates a "brittle point of failure." High-parameter models are expensive and exhibit high latency, while smaller models may lack the reasoning capabilities required for complex tasks. Model ensembles allow architects to distribute workload across multiple specialized models, balancing performance, cost, and reliability. By treating models as modular components rather than monoliths, platform engineers can achieve higher system-wide robustness.
